clue.text: Chap over the way has a lot of animals

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a chap is a man, referred to as he
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A man on the other side of the road owns a great many animals.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' puts HE above RD, so HE comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of cattle or similar beasts kept or moving together is a collective noun for a lot of animals.

definitions.meaning: to fail to catch, hit or understand something
a title for a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Someone fails to win the girl they wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to grasp or catch something is a near synonym of not getting it, and the title for an unmarried woman doubles as a word for a girl.

clue.text: Stomach-turning experience ending — unable to speak

indicators.note: turning means the word for stomach is read from right to left

parts.note: tum is an informal word for the stomach

indicators.note: ending picks out the final letter of the word experience

explanation.surface: A nauseating ordeal leaves someone speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach-turning' looks like one word meaning nauseating; split it, and 'turning' acts only on the stomach word, while 'ending' takes the last letter of 'experience'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone silent and without the power of speech is described this way.

definitions.meaning: making something level or smooth, flattening it out
the period at the close of the day, before night

explanation.surface: A routine settles into a set hour of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Levelling something out is making it smooth and regular, and the late part of the day before night is a time of day.

definitions.meaning: bringing a charge against someone, blaming them
a grammatical case, the one used for the direct object of a verb

explanation.surface: Someone is charged in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusing look is charging someone with wrongdoing, and in Latin or German grammar the objective case of a noun has this name.

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour
to quaver is to tremble, especially of a voice

explanation.surface: A notice that a house is shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: A SEMI is a British semi-detached house, one of a pair joined by a shared wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixteenth note in music, half the length of an eighth note, is this kind of note.

parts.note: something bloody is covered in red

indicators.note: catching means the animal word holds the river letter inside it

parts.note: a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: A blood-stained creature seizes a river bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin, with its red-orange chest, is a familiar British bird known by this name.

definitions.meaning: a cloth tube on a pole at an airfield showing which way the wind blows

explanation.surface: A weathervane is described as a smash success.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric cone at an airfield is a windsock, shortened here, and a punch is also called by the same informal word.

clue.text: Wearing vest and just one diamond?

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
clothes you are wearing are on you

explanation.surface: A man in a vest wears a single diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games such as bridge, a hand holding just one card of a suit has that suit as a lone card; the question mark flags the card sense of 'diamond'.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a lone card in a suit is so called, so a hand with only one diamond holds this.

clue.text: Made out it was forcibly rescinded

indicators.note: forcibly suggests the letters of rescinded are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone noticed that a decision had been overturned by force.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out something is to perceive or detect it, the past tense matching made out.

definitions.meaning: a tom is a male feline
short for catamaran, a twin-hulled boat

explanation.surface: A boat belonging to a man named Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male of a feline pet, and a catamaran is often shortened to this word for a boat.

clue.text: Grammarian has this word for things

definitions.text: Grammarian has this word for things

parts.words: Grammarian has this word for things
parts.note: the term a grammar teacher uses for a naming word, one denoting a person, place or thing

explanation.surface: A grammar expert has a term for objects.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of speech that names a thing, place or person has this grammatical label.

indicators.note: turned round means the word for the rock is read backwards

parts.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, shortened to Gib

explanation.surface: A huge boulder is rolled over.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibraltar is nicknamed the Rock, and GIB is its everyday short form; 'turned round' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and big are straightforward synonyms describing great size.

clue.text: Upper classes go to composer who avoids hard stuff

parts.note: A and B are the top social grades in British market research
Sir John Stainer was an English composer of church music

explanation.surface: Upper-class people visit a composer who is teetotal.
explanation.walkthrough: A and B are the highest bands in the British social grading system. 'Hard stuff' is strong drink; the definition reads 'one who avoids' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller, someone who refuses alcohol, is described as this, the hard stuff being spirits.

clue.text: One offering you a starry future

definitions.text: One offering you a starry future

parts.words: One offering you a starry future
parts.note: seems to promise fame, but describes someone who forecasts your life from the stars

explanation.surface: Someone promises to make you a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A horoscope writer predicts events from the positions of stars and planets.

parts.note: seems to describe someone who cannot hear rock music, but means completely without hearing, like a stone

explanation.surface: Someone cannot bear to hear rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' seems to be music; it is the stone that is utterly unhearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally deaf, with no more hearing than a lump of rock, is expressed by this phrase.

clue.text: His cattle stampeded, running and jumping

indicators.note: stampeded cattle scatter wildly, so the letters of his cattle are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer's herd bolted, charging and leaping about.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field sports, such as sprinting and the long jump, go under this name.

clue.text: Storyteller of some skill, I argue

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone claims a narrator has a certain talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is a euphemism for fibbing, so a storyteller can be someone who tells untruths.

clue.text: Spot her composing part of ode

indicators.note: composing means putting the letters of spot her together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman is seen writing a section of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: In a Greek ode, the first section sung by the chorus is called by this name.

clue.text: He may hope for a major promotion

definitions.text: He may hope for a major promotion

parts.words: He may hope for a major promotion
parts.note: seems to describe any ambitious employee, but the next army rank up is literally major

explanation.surface: An ambitious worker hopes to rise a long way up the ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: An army officer of this rank is next in line to be made a major.

clue.text: The end of the pork queue

definitions.meaning: literally the hind appendage of a pig, the animal pork comes from
a queue is a plait of hair hanging down the back

explanation.surface: The last of the meat in a line of shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's curly tail is the rear end of a pork animal, and a queue is an old word for a braid of hair hanging behind.

indicators.note: say signals that the word for mortgage is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a mortgage is a loan for buying property

explanation.surface: A single person has taken out a home loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary, single and on one's own all mean the same thing.

definitions.meaning: a bare living, just enough to survive
the state of being alive, life itself

explanation.surface: The bare subsistence of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bare living is often called a subsistence-level life, and simply being or living is the fact of being alive.

explanation.surface: A goal of reaching the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal or purpose can be called this, and so can the point where something stops.

parts.note: to do something is to make or carry it out

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside some time for a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a short form of Dorothy, a common crossword girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet form of the name Dorothy, apt for a small girl.

indicators.note: pinning has the king placed first, as though fastening the medal behind

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A monarch pins a decoration on a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch; R is Rex, Latin for king.
explanation.definitionFit: A long flowing gown is a ceremonial dress.

clue.text: Falsely tried in court, getting ban

indicators.note: falsely suggests the letters of tried in are put in a wrong, rearranged order

explanation.surface: A wrongful trial results in a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal prohibition, especially one issued by a court or church, is the noun here.

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of dire are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Serious problems while on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey on a horse, bike or vehicle is to travel.

definitions.meaning: in Scotland and Ireland a small island is called by this name

explanation.surface: A very small island.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scottish place names a small island is an inch, as in Inchcolm; the question mark flags the unusual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of length about 2.5 centimetres stands for a very small amount, and the Scottish word for an islet is the same.

parts.note: too means excessively
T is a grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tense driver leans on the horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A short blast on a car horn or trumpet is the verb here.

parts.note: a worker bee, the most common crossword worker
F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil grades

explanation.surface: An employee receives good quality meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat from cattle is sold under this name.

clue.text: Pr man has to turn fast at entrance in court

parts.note: to spin is to turn rapidly

indicators.note: in signals the court abbreviation goes inside the word for entrance

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A publicist must whirl quickly when entering a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' seems to mean firmly fixed, but it pairs with 'turn' to mean whirl rapidly; 'in' puts the court abbreviation inside the entrance word.
explanation.definitionFit: A public relations adviser who puts a favourable slant on news is known by this phrase.
